results.q: What happens when the slave responds with an ACKNOWLEDGE exception?
answer: This is handled in ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:158): it checks `readAgain` (`readAgain = exceptionResponse.SlaveExceptionCode == SlaveExceptionCodes.Acknowledge`, line 156), and when that is true it calls LoggingExtensions.Debug() and calls ModbusTransport.Sleep() and calls WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get().

results.q: What happens when a response has an unexpected function code?
answer: This is handled in ModbusTransport.ValidateResponse() (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:250): it checks `request.FunctionCode != response.FunctionCode`, and when that is true it calls FunctionCode.get() and calls new IOException() and throws `new IOException(msg)`, so the rest of ModbusTransport.ValidateResponse() is skipped and the exception goes to its caller.
Because it returns early, these do not happen in this case: SlaveAddress.get() — the previous values stay in place.

ModbusTransport.ValidateResponse() is called by ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() inside a try block (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:176); its `catch (Exception)` handler (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:195) checks `(e is SocketException socketException && socketException.SocketErrorCode != SocketError.TimedOut) || (e.InnerException is SocketException innerSocketException && innerSocketException.SocketErrorCode != SocketError.TimedOut)` (line 197); if true it throws the exception again; then it checks `e is FormatException || e is NotImplementedException || e is TimeoutException || e is IOException || e is SocketException` (line 202); if true it calls LoggingExtensions.Error(), Exception.GetType, ModbusTransport.Sleep(), WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get(); otherwise it throws the exception again; then it checks `attempt++ > _retries` (line 210); if true it throws the exception again.
Bad input is also rejected in other places: ModbusTransport.ShouldRetryResponse() rejects it when `request.FunctionCode != response.FunctionCode` (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:279).

results.q: What happens when a request times out?
answer: Losing the data is detected in ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() (NModbus/IO/ModbusTransport.cs:202), which checks `e is FormatException || e is NotImplementedException || e is TimeoutException || e is IOException || e is SocketException`.

When that happens it calls LoggingExtensions.Error() (which calls IModbusLogger.Log(LoggingLevel.Error, message) (line 33)); calls Exception.GetType; calls ModbusTransport.Sleep() (which calls Task.Wait (line 331)); calls WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get().

ModbusTransport.UnicastMessage<T>() also stops early when `attempt++ > _retries` (line 210), which skips ModbusTransport.Sleep(), WaitToRetryMilliseconds.get() — so without fresh valid data it does not reach those calls either.
